comment: If you want an easy class, I would highly recommend American Studies. If you want an interesting class, do not take this class. Professor Brauer loves to hear himself speak, and everyone in the class just did stuff on their laptops. Get an A if you do any resemblance to work, but if you want to form your own opinions, do not take this class.
Very long lectures and difficult to pick out useful details. Lots of text and readings are necessary for writing assignments. Cool guy, but difficult to study or know what is important.

Professor Brauer loves what he does. He's fun and very knowledgeable on what he teaches. His lectures are all about reading books/documents, so have a decent idea of them since he'll call on you. Only 3 papers, so take if you're a good writer. He gets off topic making small talk mid class, but it's a reflection of him caring for his students.

Highly recommend. He is a super chill guy. Really wants to gets to know his students and is very understanding. Had a few papers but none were too bad and easy grader. If you need a gen ed english class take modernism and in the city.
He was a very chill FYS teacher, had 2-3 papers and an in class writing. Easy to talk to outside class and likes it when people participate. Not a lot of work, need to buy 2 books
Love this class! It's smart and interesting and keeps your attention. Strong recommendation

He is a tough grader early on. But those grades don't reflect your overall grade. 

I hadn't really seen the type of grades that he gave me early. But it made sense by the end and I was a better writer because of his comments.

Outside of the classroom he is very available and definitely tries to get to know you to help you more effectively.
would go on tangents about weird stories and did not give good feedback to grading.

I took the Crime in America FYS with Brauer and it wasn't what I expected but it was good. You have to read/watch the movies or you won't be ready for the cold calls. The essay prompts were confusing but similar for almost every unit but he clears it up a lot and is helpful during his office hours. Super chill dude but not a class about true-crime.

Pretty nice guy, and very accommodating of extensions and that type of thing. I found him to be a pretty easy grader, but I know a lot of people who said otherwise. His prompts were confusing and often repetitive, but they were fairly easy to write for. H and V was a decent class, just boring. No need to pay attention, I usually did homework.

A very interesting FYS class, which was really useful in actually developing my writing abilities through the topic. He was also an extremely approachable professor and helped both myself and others in the class with various personal issues and was very flexible with trying to make sure we could manage the workload of the class. Great guy.

Brauer is a nice guy but a bad professor. He spends the whole class lecturing and going on random tangents not at all related to the course. The essays are not clear unless you go in during office hours and have him explain. He wasn't always available during set office hours but was good about picking another time that works for you

Professor Brauer is a nice guy, but spends the entire class talking. He asks maybe one question a class for people to listen to, and talks for the rest of the class. Prompts for his papers are extremely unclear, and he is pretty difficult to reach outside of class. He does a good job making you write in an authentic way, but grades very strictly.

Brauer is a very knowledgable professor. His FYS class, though he lectures for most of it about random topics, is very insightful into the world of crime. The essays are very clearly laid out and he's a pretty good guy. Be prepared though for him to cold-call you to ask questions during class, he is not afraid to call you out either.
